en: In contrast, the translucent quality of silk enabled underpaintings made on one side to be visible from the other side. In the case of the Mahāmāyūrī banner, black underpainting appears only on one side, therefore designating that side as the recto (see fig. 1). This effect is most visible in areas of bare skin and particularly in the deity’s arms and upturned hand (fig. 9).18 From visual observation, the contours of the underpainting were carefully filled in with colored pigments, after which a deep red outline was painted over the black underpainting, partially obscuring it. The other side of the painting bears no trace of black underpainting, only red outlines, which demonstrates that the silk was sufficiently sheer so as to render the black outlines visible on the verso (see fig. 7). On the verso, the same
zh: 相比之下，丝绸的半透明特性使得一侧的底色从另一侧也能看到。在孔雀明王旗帜的情况下，黑色底色仅出现在一侧，因此将该侧称为正面（见图1）。这种效果在裸露皮肤区域尤为明显，尤其是在神像的手臂和翻转的手上（图9）。通过视觉观察可知，底色的轮廓被彩色颜料仔细填充，随后在黑色底色上绘制了深红色轮廓，部分遮住了黑色底色。画作的另一侧没有黑色底色的痕迹，只有红色轮廓，这表明丝绸的透明度足够高，使得黑色轮廓在背面也能显现出来（见图7）。在背面，同样的情况依然存在。

en: The garment is fastened around the waist with green, red, and purple cloth, and a double-faced blue- and-red scarf billows artfully along the length of the deity’s body.20 As important Silk Road commodities, the representation of silk textiles in this painted banner merits attention. The detailed representation is also evident in a separate group of painted banners, which attests to the vibrancy of banner-painting traditions along the southern silk route, and in particular, the artistic impact of the Buddhist kingdom of Khotan (fig. 10).
zh: 这件服饰以绿色、红色和紫色布料系在腰间，一条双面蓝色与红色围巾则优雅地飘扬在神像的身形上。作为重要的丝绸之路商品，这幅绘有丝绸织物的旗帜值得关注。另一组绘有图案的旗帜也展现了详细的描绘，这证明了南方丝绸路线上的旗帜绘画传统十分活跃，尤其是霍坦佛教王国的艺术影响力（图10）。

en: SILK BANNERS ON THE SILK ROAD Of the silk banners recovered by Stein from Mogao Cave 17, a group of ten that were gathered during his second expedition serves as a particularly instructive point of comparison for the Mahāmāyūrī banner. The group is now divided between the British Museum in London (three paintings) and the National Museum of India in New Delhi (seven paintings).21 The works display stylistic traits of Khotanese and Himalayan artistic traditions, the latter of which reflects on the Tibetan occupation of Khotan between the seventh and ninth centuries. Like the Mahāmāyūrī banner, one from this latter group is inscribed on the verso. The Tibetan inscription identifies the deity represented on the recto as Vajrapān.i (fig. 11).22 The writing of inscriptions on the verso rather than on the recto is more commonly seen
zh: 丝绸路上的丝绸旗帜 斯坦因在莫高第17窟发现的十幅丝绸旗帜中，有三幅是他第二次考察时采集的，这些旗帜对于孔雀明王的旗帜具有重要的对比意义。目前，这些作品分别藏于伦敦大英博物馆（三幅）和新德里印度国家博物馆（七幅）。这些作品展现了和田与喜马拉雅艺术传统的风格特征，后者反映了七至九世纪西藏对和田的统治情况。与孔雀明王旗帜一样，其中一幅作品也刻有背面文字。藏文铭文指出正面所绘神像为金刚萨埵（图11）。在背面刻写铭文而非正面则更为常见。

en: The meaning of the extant part of the inscription is otherwise clear: an official with the title of āmāca, possibly named Yarais.a, donated something “in love of bodhi of the Four Assemblies.” The verb used here, hatīś-, has the general meaning “to give.”30 But in religious contexts, it often means more specifically “to donate,” which better fits the context of this inscription.31 The inscription does not specify what this āmāca official donated, but it is very likely that it was the painting on which this inscription was written. en: other titles to denote an official of the highest status in the government of Khotan.34 Because of the centrality of this title in the Khotanese bureaucracy, it also appeared in Chinese (amozhi) and Tibetan (a-ma-cha), the languages of the two empires that ruled Khotan between the seventh and ninth centuries. In Khotanese documents from Dunhuang, most of which date to the tenth century, āmāca remained an important title.35 For instance, in the preface to the Jātakastava, the author of the text prays for the people of Khotan: after mentioning the king, the queen, and the princes, the author continues to list “the great prime minister (Khotanese: tsai-syām. ; Chinese: zaixiang), āmāca the servant of the god,” as well as “the good, the bad, and the middle, all the people in the country.”36 From the hierarchical sequencing of the prayer it is clear that in the tenth century, āmāca, while a lower title than prime minister, was still one of the most important titles in Khotan. It is therefore fitting that an āmāca should have had the means to commission such a lavish silk painting. But how did a painting commissioned by a Khotanese official end up in the library cave in Dunhuang? To answer this question, we need to place the life of this painting in the context of the political history of Central Asia in the ninth to the tenth century.
zh: 其他标题用于指代霍坦政府中最高级别的官员。由于这一头衔在霍坦官僚体系中的中心性地位，它也出现在第七至九世纪统治霍坦的两个帝国所使用的语言——汉语和藏语中。在来自敦煌的霍坦文献中，大部分可追溯到十世纪，āmāca仍是一个重要的头衔。例如，在《本生经》的序言中，文本作者为霍坦人民祈祷：在提到国王、王后和王子之后，作者继续列举“伟大的首相（霍坦语：tsai-syām；汉语：宰相），作为神之仆人的āmāca”，以及“善良的、邪恶的、中等的人，这个国家中的所有人”。从祈祷文的等级排序来看，显然在十世纪时，虽然āmāca比首相处于较低级别，但它仍然是霍坦最重要的头衔之一。因此，一个拥有āmāca头衔的人能够委托绘制如此精美的丝绸画也就不足为奇了。但是，一幅由霍坦官员委托绘制的画作究竟是如何被保存在敦煌的藏经洞中的呢？要回答这个问题，我们需要将这幅画的流传历史置于九至十世纪中亚政治历史的背景下进行考察。

en: However, this does not mean it was not from Stein’s second expedition. By no means had all the material been conserved at this time and some remained in a state that conservators at the time did not feel able to tackle. In these early years, many of the original bundles are marked as having been returned from conservation as untreatable.66 So, it is possible that the painting was among the second expedition material kept at the British Museum in an unidentified state. Furthermore, material from Stein’s third expedition (1916–18) was sent to British India to be conserved, listed, and prepared for acquisition. Stein had acquired more material from Dunhuang on this expedition, and while there is no evidence of paintings or banners among them, it is not impossible that some of the material included unconserved fragments, such as the banner.67
zh: 然而，这并不意味着这件绘幡一定不属于斯坦因第二次考察所得。当时，远非所有材料都完成了保护处理，有些材料的状况甚至使当时的修复人员感到无从下手。在早期记录中，许多原装卷束被标记为因无法处理而从修复环节退回。〔66〕因此，这幅绘画可能属于第二次考察所得材料，只是以尚未辨识的状态留在大英博物馆。此外，斯坦因第三次考察（1916—1918）所得材料，被送往英属印度接受保护处理、列单并准备入藏。斯坦因在此次考察中又从敦煌取得了一些材料；虽然没有证据表明其中有绘画或幡，但不能排除其中包含尚未修复的残片，例如这件绘幡。〔67〕
